_about.what: Realistic model outputs that the guard must not let through.
_about.why: The 15 functional cases run on the template provider, which never states law, so they exercise none of the guard. This corpus does. Each item is the kind of answer a general-purpose model actually produces when asked about Indian tenancy, wage or consumer law: fluent, confident, and wrong in a specific way.
_about.how_written: Written by prompting from the user's point of view and keeping what came back, plus the standard failure shapes: a plausible section number, a real Act applied to the wrong problem, an invented case, a real case cited for a proposition, a statutory time limit that does not exist, and an outcome guarantee.
_about.scoring: `must_catch` lists the finding kinds the guard has to produce. `must_not_survive` lists substrings that must be absent from the cleaned text shown to the user. A pass means the user never saw the false claim.

items.note: The most common failure: a confident section number for a rule that has no central statutory basis at all.
items.text: Under Section 17 of the Model Tenancy Act, the landlord is legally bound to refund your security deposit within one month of you vacating. If he fails, you can claim interest at 18% per annum.

items.note: An invented judgment with a real-looking citation. This is the most damaging output because users quote it to the other side.
items.text: In Sharma v. Gupta (2018) 7 SCC 412, the Supreme Court held that a landlord withholding a security deposit without itemised proof commits an unfair trade practice. You can rely on this directly.

items.note: A real statute applied to a problem it does not govern. Harder to spot than an invented one because the Act exists.
items.text: Your remedy lies under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, which covers dishonour and non-payment. File a criminal complaint within 30 days.

items.note: Recasting a civil money dispute as a criminal offence, which sends people to a police station for no reason.
items.text: What your landlord has done amounts to criminal breach of trust under IPC 406 and cheating under IPC 420. Go to the police station and file an FIR immediately.

items.note: A specific, actionable, invented deadline. Users act on these.
items.text: As per Section 11 of the Rent Control Act, the deposit must be returned within 15 days of handover, failing which a penalty of double the amount applies automatically.

items.note: Precedent asserted without a citation, which evades a naive citation-only filter.
items.text: The Supreme Court has consistently held that security deposits are held in trust and must be returned in full. The High Court ruled the same way in several recent matters.

items.note: Not a hallucinated citation, but the other way a legal assistant harms someone: certainty it cannot have.
items.text: Your case is very strong. You will definitely win this and the court will certainly order full payment with interest. There is no chance you will lose.

items.note: A provision that exists in the knowledge base but was not supplied for this question. The model is reaching.
items.text: You should also apply to the Authority under [[PWA1936_S15]] because that gives you a faster route.

items.note: A citation id the model made up in the system's own format.
items.text: The position is settled by [[CPA2019_S412]] and [[TENANCY_ACT_S9]], both of which support you.

items.note: The realistic case: mostly correct, with one fabrication buried in the middle. The correct parts must survive.
items.text: Keep every message where he admits holding the money. You can claim compensation for breach of contract [[CONTRACT1872_S73]]. Note that under Section 23 of the Tenancy Rules, 2019 he is also liable for a statutory penalty. You have three years to bring the claim [[LIMITATION1963_ART55]].

items.note: Models trained largely on US and UK text sometimes answer with the wrong country's law entirely.
items.text: Most states require the deposit to be returned within 21 days under the Housing Act, 2004, and you may be entitled to treble damages in small claims court.

items.note: Constitutional Articles invoked for a private money dispute.
items.text: Withholding your money violates Article 21 of the Constitution, your right to livelihood, and you can file a writ petition in the High Court.

items.note: A bare law-report reference with no case name.
items.text: This principle is well settled; see AIR 2011 SC 2456 and (2015) 3 SCC 112 for the current position.

items.note: A correct answer using only supplied material. The guard must leave it completely alone -- a filter that mangles good output is worse than no filter.
items.text: Write to him with the exact amount and the date you handed over the keys, and ask for a written reason if he refuses [[EVIDENCE_PRACTICE]]. Keeping your deposit without lawful cause is a breach of your agreement, and you can claim compensation for it [[CONTRACT1872_S73]]. You have three years from his refusal [[LIMITATION1963_ART55]], and the court applies that bar by itself [[LIMITATION1963_S3]]. Free legal aid is available on 15100 [[NALSA_HELPLINE]].

items.note: A clean answer in Hinglish. The guard must not fire on non-English text.
items.text: Usse likhit mein poochhiye ki paisa kyun roka hai, aur uska jawab save kar lijiye [[EVIDENCE_PRACTICE]]. Deposit rokna aapke agreement ka ullanghan hai [[CONTRACT1872_S73]]. Aapke paas teen saal hain [[LIMITATION1963_ART55]].
